title: How a model is made
case: Follow one language model from raw text to the pinned version the flagship scene calls.
disclaimer: Teaching simulation. The stages are real; the scale, numbers, names and examples are illustrative and far smaller than any production model. No part of this page trains or calls a model.

page.label: Second lesson.
page.intro: One model, followed from raw text to a released version: what it learns from, what training actually adjusts, what fine-tuning and alignment add, and what evaluation has to show before release.
page.outcomesIntro: Release is a decision made on evidence. These are the ways this build can end.

interventions.label: Skew the training data
interventions.help: One group of writers dominates the corpus and others are rare.

interventions.label: Train too long on too little text
interventions.help: A small corpus, many passes over it.

interventions.label: Skip the preference stage
interventions.help: The fine-tuned model goes straight to evaluation.

released.label: Released
released.text: Released as a pinned version after meeting its evaluation criteria. From here, what changes per call is the context; monitoring in use decides when a new version is needed.

held_back.label: Held back
held_back.text: Not released: evaluation found a problem the release criteria do not allow. Holding back is the control working. The next attempt starts from the data or the recipe.

frame.title: Where this fits
frame.narration: The model in the flagship scene is one kind of AI: inside machine learning, inside deep learning, a large language model. This lesson follows how such a model is made, long before any application calls it.

collect.title: Collect and filter text
collect.narration: A large body of text is gathered, cleaned and deduplicated. A held-out slice is set aside and never trained on. The bars show who and what is represented; gaps here become weak spots later.

collect_skewed.title: Collect text, one group dominates
collect_skewed.narration: The text is gathered and cleaned, but one group of writers dominates and others are rare. Nothing fails yet. The skew stays silent until someone measures by group.

tokenize.title: Cut the text into tokens
tokenize.narration: A tokenizer splits text into tokens: whole words, parts of words, characters. Whether 'cracked' is one token or two depends on the tokenizer.

embed.title: Turn each token into numbers
embed.narration: Each token is looked up in a learned embedding table and becomes a vector, a long list of numbers. During training, tokens used in similar ways drift near each other.

architecture.title: Up through the stack of blocks
architecture.narration: The vectors pass up through many identical blocks. In each, attention lets every token weigh the others, then a small neural network transforms each one. The top of the stack scores every possible next token.

neuron.title: Inside one unit
neuron.narration: Zoom into one unit of that network: multiply each input by a weight, add them up, apply a simple function. The weights are parameters. At the start of training they are random.

predict.title: Guess the next token
predict.narration: Training shows real text with the next token hidden: 'The lamp arrived ___'. The model gives every candidate a probability, for example cracked 12%, broken 9%, late 4%. The numbers here are illustrative.

loss.title: Measure how wrong it was
loss.narration: The text said 'cracked'. The loss is one number for how little probability the model gave the right token. The training algorithm's whole aim is to make this number smaller.

backprop.title: Adjust every parameter a little
backprop.narration: Backpropagation works out, for every parameter, which direction would have lowered the loss. Each one moves a tiny step that way. No person edits a rule; the numbers shift.

repeat.title: Repeat across the corpus
repeat.narration: The loop runs an enormous number of times. Training loss falls, and loss on the held-out slice falls with it: the patterns carry over to text the model has not seen.

repeat_overfit.title: Too many passes over too little text
repeat_overfit.narration: With a small corpus and many passes, training loss keeps falling but held-out loss turns upward. The model is memorising its examples instead of learning patterns that carry over.

checkpoint.title: Save the base model
checkpoint.narration: The architecture and its learned parameters are saved as a checkpoint, base-v0. It continues text fluently, but a pretrained model is not inherently good at answering questions or following instructions.

finetune.title: Fine-tune on worked examples
finetune.narration: The base model is trained further on request and good-answer pairs written by people. It starts to answer like an assistant, and to copy any habits in those examples.

align.title: Train toward preferred answers
align.narration: People, or a model guided by written principles, compare pairs of answers. A preference model learns those choices and reinforcement learning shifts the model toward the preferred ones. Wanted behaviour becomes more likely. It is not guaranteed.

align_skipped.title: The preference stage is skipped
align_skipped.narration: To save time, the preference stage is skipped and the fine-tuned model goes straight to evaluation.

evaluate.title: Test on what it never trained on
evaluate.narration: The candidate is tested on held-out tasks, on requests it should decline, and by group to look for uneven quality. Every release criterion is met.

eval_bias_fail.title: Uneven quality between groups
eval_bias_fail.narration: The average score looks fine. Scores by group show the model misreads the under-represented writers. A release criterion fails, and the fix is in the data, not the prompt.

eval_overfit_fail.title: It does not generalise
eval_overfit_fail.narration: On held-out tasks the candidate scores far below its training results. It memorised. The fix is more varied data or fewer passes, then train again.

eval_unaligned_fail.title: Answers it should not give
eval_unaligned_fail.narration: On the decline tests the candidate goes along with requests it should refuse and is curt with upset customers. A release criterion fails.

release.title: Pin and release a version
release.narration: The passing checkpoint is released under a fixed version name, and applications pin it: this is the model card in the flagship scene. Its parameters no longer change. Each call gets a fresh context.
